historical_reviews.deepseek: The single OOB read is relevant but does not demonstrate the required interfaces or bind the temperature to the installed BF3 DPU.

original_test_intent: Verify the installed BlueField-3 adapter's chip-temperature resource across IB/OOB SDR, IB/OOB Sensor List and BMC Web, including stable DPU identity, description, reading, units, status and freshness against the approved BF3 silicon SPEC.
original_method: Prove common BMC/SUT identity and map the sensor to the installed BF3 adapter, record DPU mode and workload context, collect complete command views and the exact protected Web row within a bounded interval, then normalize fields and compare to chip limits without clearing logs or resetting/reconfiguring the DPU.
manual_activity: A platform/network reviewer approves the BF3 adapter-to-sensor mapping, DPU operating context and junction-temperature limits, then confirms the protected Web row and five-view result.
required_inputs: DPU mode, firmware and workload state
safety_requirements: Do not reset/reconfigure or update the BF3 DPU
Bind the sensor to the exact BF3 adapter
Exclude BF3 transceiver and unrelated chip resources
Capture complete lists and page context
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and BF3 adapter identity
Record DPU mode, firmware and workload context
Collect full IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists
Capture the protected BF3 chip Web row
engineer_actions: Approve BF3 adapter/sensor map and chip SPEC
Resolve absent, duplicate or divergent resources

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The OOB `sensor get` can sample a named BF3 resource but does not prove adapter identity, IB coverage, complete lists or Web agreement; the truncated SDR fallback may omit it.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture complete IB/OOB SDR and Sensor views plus the exact Web entry, keyed to verified BF3 adapter identity and DPU operating context.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Five interfaces, one BF3 chip sensor and timestamp metadata remain; generic clear and partial fallback evidence are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate a single BF3 junction-temperature row across five timestamped views using adapter PCIe/board identity, firmware/mode and workload context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable DPU identity and operating-state context instead of relying on a generic `grep chip` match.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Generic chip filtering may return another controller or a plausible but unrelated sensor while the installed BF3 resource is missing.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BF3 operating mode and workload can affect junction temperature, so comparison requires the SPEC's applicable state and tolerance.

project_override_considerations: Define the installed BF3 adapter identity, telemetry source, DPU mode/load context, fields, limits and tolerance. The following BF3 transceiver case remains independent; private Script use requires pinned review.
expected_evidence: BF3 PCIe/board identity, DPU firmware/mode and sensor map
Workload context and approved junction-temperature SPEC
Complete decoded IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists
Protected BF3 chip Web row and page context
No-BF3/SDR/thermal mutation or log-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target the BF3 chip sensor across five views. Generic log clearing and DeepSeek's partial collection are method defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The adapter identity, access, telemetry mapping and SPEC are identifiable prerequisites. Execution becomes BLOCKED only if the chip sensor cannot be bound to the installed BF3 after those inputs are obtained.

review_improvement: Makes the BF3 result DPU-specific by requiring adapter identity, mode/load context and all five views, while excluding the neighboring optical-module resource.
independent_technical_reasoning: BlueField-3 is a programmable DPU whose silicon temperature varies with its operating mode and workload. A name match alone cannot show that the reading belongs to the installed adapter or is evaluated under an applicable limit; adapter identity and state must accompany the five-view correlation.
